query: Should I add any bond exposure at all, or stay close to 100% equity given my horizon?

recommendations.title: Maintain Aggressive 100% Equity Allocation
recommendations.summary: Given your age (30), 15+ year horizon, aggressive risk tolerance (9/10), stable income, and low liquidity needs, maintaining near-100% equity exposure is optimal for wealth accumulation and FIRE goals.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your profile is ideal for maximum equity exposure: (1) 15-year horizon provides ample time to recover from market downturns, (2) stable $195K income with only $18K debt provides substantial buffer, (3) emergency fund covers short-term needs, (4) loss comfort of 9/10 indicates true risk capacity. Bonds would likely reduce your expected returns from ~9-10% to ~7-8% annually, potentially adding 2-3 years to your FIRE timeline. Historical data shows 100% equity portfolios outperform 80/20 or 60/40 allocations over 15+ year periods. The opportunity cost of bond 'safety' is significant at your age - approximately $400K-600K in foregone gains by retirement. Your current 10% cash allocation already provides sufficient stability buffer.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current equity allocation; avoid adding bonds

recommendations.title: Reduce Tech Concentration Risk
recommendations.summary: Your 65% technology sector allocation creates significant concentration risk. Diversify into value, international, and small-cap equities while maintaining aggressive equity stance.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: While staying 100% equity is appropriate, your 65% tech weighting (combined with tech-heavy QQQ and individual FAANG holdings) creates unnecessary single-sector risk. Tech sector drawdowns can exceed 50% (2000-2002: -78%, 2022: -33%). Diversification across sectors and geographies can reduce volatility by 15-20% without sacrificing long-term returns. Recommend adding: (1) VTV or AVUV for value/small-cap exposure (15-20%), (2) VXUS or VEA for international diversification (20-25%), (3) reducing individual tech stocks to 15-20% of portfolio. This maintains aggressive growth orientation while reducing single-sector career risk (your income and investments both tied to tech). Your FIRE goal benefits more from consistent compounding than from concentrated bets.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reallocate 20-25% from tech into value, small-cap, and international equity

recommendations.title: Reduce Crypto Allocation to 2-3%
recommendations.summary: Your 5% crypto allocation ($9,000) is appropriate for aggressive profile but consider reducing to 2-3% to limit extreme volatility while maintaining asymmetric upside potential.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: While crypto can provide portfolio diversification and asymmetric returns, 5% allocation introduces significant volatility (80%+ drawdowns) that doesn't align with systematic FIRE planning. BTC has shown -85% peak-to-trough declines and 300%+ annual volatility. A 2-3% allocation ($3,600-5,400) still provides meaningful exposure to potential 10-20x returns over 15 years while limiting downside impact. If BTC goes to zero, you lose $3,600 vs $9,000 - meaningful difference. If it 10x's, you still capture $36K-54K gain. Reallocate the freed 2-3% ($5,400) into diversified equity positions (international or value). This optimization improves your risk-adjusted returns and Sharpe ratio. Crypto should be treated as a satellite speculation position, not core holding. Your $195K income allows for continued monthly crypto purchases if desired without overweighting portfolio.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reduce BTC position from 5% to 2-3%; reallocate to diversified equities

recommendations.title: Maximize Tax-Advantaged Account Contributions
recommendations.summary: Ensure you're maximizing 401k ($23,000), Roth IRA ($7,000), and consider mega backdoor Roth if available. Tax optimization is critical for FIRE goals.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: At $195K income with only $5,500 monthly expenses, you have $7,750/month available for investment. Tax-advantaged accounts provide 22-24% immediate 'return' via tax savings plus decades of tax-free growth. Prioritize: (1) Max 401k contribution ($23K = $1,917/month) especially if employer match available, (2) Backdoor Roth IRA ($7K = $583/month), (3) Mega backdoor Roth if plan allows (additional $43.5K = $3,625/month). Combined $73.5K annual tax-advantaged contributions accelerates FIRE timeline by 2-3 years versus taxable investing. Within these accounts, maintain aggressive equity allocation (VTI, VXUS, sector ETFs). Use taxable brokerage for remaining $20K+ annual savings. For FIRE at 45-47, you'll need substantial tax-advantaged balance accessible via Roth conversion ladder or 72(t) distributions. Front-loading these accounts now is mathematically optimal given your stable high income and low current expenses.
recommendations.suggested_action: Verify maxing all tax-advantaged accounts; redirect cash flow accordingly
